basic_identification.full_title: Agro Textiles — Insect Nets for Agriculture and Horticulture Purposes — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agrotech Applications (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Technical Textiles for Agrotech Applications Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agrotech Applications Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the physical, mechanical, and performance requirements, along with corresponding test methods, for insect nets manufactured from UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene (HDPE) monofilament yarns. These nets are designed for agricultural and horticultural crop protection against common pests (such as aphids, whiteflies, thrips, and caterpillars) in orchards, shade net houses, and greenhouses, while reducing synthetic chemical pesticide usage.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Agrotech Textiles / Crop Protection Materials)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Insect Nets manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 16513:2016 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified agricultural insect nets in India is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic monofilament insect netting.

requirements.detail: Every roll or bundle of certified insect net must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 16513) printed on a secure label or edge tape.

The insect nets must be woven from high-strength High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) monofilament yarns. Raw yarns, dyes, and pigments must be completely non-toxic, safe for soil systems, and thoroughly UV-stabilized.
The mass per unit area (GSM) tested in accordance with IS 1964 must strictly stay within ±5 percent of the standard variety mass to prevent thin patches or weave inconsistencies.

requirements.requirement_type: Warp and Weft Weave Density (Ends and Picks)
requirements.detail: The warp yarn count (Ends per inch) and weft yarn count (Picks per inch) must be verified to ensure precise aperture spacing and hole size limits to block targeted pest species.
The net must show high resistance to wind pressure and mechanical stress. Initial breaking strength (Dry and Wet) in both warp and weft directions must satisfy specified minimum load thresholds.

After 500 hours of UV accelerated weathering exposure, the retained breaking strength in both warp and weft directions must satisfy a specified minimum percentage of the initial breaking strength to guarantee a service life of at least 4 to 5 years under intense solar radiation.

The woven monofilament structure must resist localized physical pressure (e.g., from heavy rainfall or wind gusts), demonstrating high bursting strength when tested as per hydraulic/pneumatic methods of IS 1966.
The netting must achieve adequate air permeability limits to ensure proper micro-climate ventilation, preventing temperature spikes and high humidity inside greenhouses.
The pigments used in colored nets (such as milky white, clear, or green) must demonstrate a lightfastness rating of at least 7 to 8 to prevent sun-bleaching and structural degradation.
Standard rolls must be securely wound and packed to prevent physical damage during shipment. Standard commercial roll sizes include widths of 1.5 m or 3 m, and lengths of 50 m or 100 m.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16513 : 2016 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene (HDPE) monofilament insect nets used in agriculture and horticulture to protect crops against pests like aphids, whiteflies, and caterpillars. Under India's statutory Agro Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all insect nets manufactured, imported, or sold in the country must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard classifies nets based on mesh count into Type I (30 mesh), Type II/II A (40 mesh), and Type III (50 mesh). Amendment No. 3 (October 2024) refines the standard by introducing a heavyweight 40 mesh variant (Type II A, 125 g/m²) and establishing a strict ±5% mass tolerance (GSM) tested under IS 1964. The standard enforces detailed mechanical and physical benchmarks—including initial breaking strength, minimum retained breaking strength after 500 hours of UV exposure, high hydraulic bursting strength, and controlled air permeability to ensure optimal ventilation and long-lasting crop protection under harsh outdoor weathering.
